name: Desktop Cube
description: Rotates the two desktops past each other like the faces of a spinning cube. This is the classic desktop switcher look.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from GL-Transitions cube by gre, MIT)

name: Desktop Dissolve
description: Dissolves the outgoing desktop into the incoming one through a field of random speckles.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Tab Dissolve
description: Every speckle of the column turns over from one tab to the other at its own moment, so the tab you left grains away into the one you picked. Raise the density for a finer grain and the fade width for a softer speckle.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Apparition
description: Window violently sucks into a swirling void with shake, twirl, and suction distortion
author: PlasmaZones

name: Flyeye
description: Faceted-lens distortion. The UV oscillates on a cosine/sine grid and settles as the surface fades.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Morph
description: Smooth warping morph transition using displacement fields
author: PlasmaZones

name: Ripple
description: An outward radial ripple using sin-modulated UV displacement with a seed-stable per-instance phase. The envelope and alpha curves differ between open and close.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Strip Carousel
description: The strip tilts like a spinning drum while it scrolls. The side the content slides toward leans away with a gentle perspective and shade, and the strip flattens back out as it settles.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Strip Chromatic
description: Chromatic aberration while the strip scrolls. The red and blue channels pull apart along the direction of travel, further the faster you scroll, and snap back together as the strip settles.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Strip Motion Blur
description: Motion blur on the scrolling strip. The blur follows the scroll speed and fades out as the strip settles.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Aura Glow
description: The window crops into a colour-shifting glowing orb that fades out, using a square-to-circle gradient with a hue-cycling rim
author: PlasmaZones

name: Circle
description: Circular reveal expanding from a slightly randomized center, with soft edge falloff.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Colour Distance
description: Pixels emerge in order of brightness, using a luminance threshold.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Desktop Fade
description: Cross-fades the outgoing virtual desktop into the incoming one when you switch desktops.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Dissolve
description: Noise-based dissolve transition with configurable grain
author: PlasmaZones

name: Fade
description: Gentle scale-and-fade transition. Opening eases scale from 0.95 to 1.0 while the window fades in. Closing eases scale from 1.0 to 0.95 while it fades out.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Fade Color
description: A phased fade where visibility ramps up with smoothstep. The Color Phase dial delays the start of the fade and matches the niri original at 0.4.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Focus
description: A camera-focus rack where the surface appears and disappears through a depth-of-field-style blur ring.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from Burn-My-Windows by Simon Schneegans, https://github.com/Schneegans/Burn-My-Windows)

name: Overexposure
description: A brightness-pumped fade where channel intensities lift over a sin-modulated envelope while alpha fades.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Soft Warp Fade
description: A subtle noise warp combined with an eased fade for a gentle, organic transition.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Tab Fade
description: Cross-fade between the two tabs of a scrolling column. The tab you left dissolves into the one you picked, both at the same size in the same place, so the column reads as one surface changing its contents rather than two windows swapping.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Flow
description: Geometry move and resize transition where the window streams into its destination zone instead of sliding across rigidly. The edge facing the target arrives first and the trailing rows lag and catch up, so the window looks like it is being poured into the slot, with the old frame cross-fading into the live content as each region settles.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Fold
description: Geometry move and resize transition where the window folds up like an accordion as it travels and unfolds flat into its destination zone. The creases run across the direction of motion and pick up a soft shadow at the peak of the fold, so the window looks like a sheet of paper tucking into the slot and opening out again once it lands.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Phosphor Stream
description: The window pours into its zone as separated luminous streams. Each stream runs on its own slightly offset clock and bows apart mid flight, carrying a different stop of the brand gradient, with ember sparks shed in the wake. The streams reunite exactly at the destination, so the settled window carries no residue.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Ripple Snap
description: Geometry move and resize transition where the window flies into its destination zone and a wave ripples across it from the edge that lands first, like a sheet snapping taut. The ripple fades out as the window settles flat into the slot.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Stretch
description: Geometry move and resize transition with an elastic, rubber-band feel. The leading edge springs into the destination zone first while the rest of the window lags and stretches taut behind it, thinning slightly as it travels, then snaps to fit with a single overshoot before settling.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Tab Flip
description: Turns the column over like a card. The tab you left narrows to its edge, and the one you picked opens out from that edge to fill the column again. Shading darkens the turn at its steepest so the card reads as solid.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Window Morph
description: Geometry move and resize transition. The window jumps to its destination instantly, and this shader animates the drawn rect from the old geometry to the new one. The content is drawn at its final size the whole way, so a snap, tile or reflow slides and crops into place with the window's pixels staying exactly as sharp as they are when it settles.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Aretha Materialize
description: The window resolves hexagon by hexagon along a diagonal data sweep, with a glowing cyan leading edge, chromatic glitch, and scanlines in the Aretha / Ghost-in-the-Shell style.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Desktop Aretha
description: Switches desktops hexagon by hexagon along a diagonal data sweep, with a glowing cyan leading edge and pink glitch flashes in the Aretha style.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Glitch
description: Digital glitch transition with RGB offset and block displacement
author: PlasmaZones

name: Matrix
description: Falling-glyph rain transition that wipes the window through a Matrix-style cascade.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from Burn-My-Windows by Schneegans, https://github.com/Schneegans/Burn-My-Windows)

name: RGB Warp
description: A vertical chromatic-aberration ripple. The RGB channels lift off the top of the window at slightly different speeds
author: PlasmaZones

name: Static Fade
description: A TV-static interference reveal. Random RGB static panels overlay the surface and ramp up in intensity at the midpoint.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: TV Glitch
description: Analog glitch artifacts. RGB shift, scanlines, and noise tear across the surface as it collapses.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from Burn-My-Windows by Simon Schneegans, https://github.com/Schneegans/Burn-My-Windows)

name: Broken Glass
description: Surface shatters into glass shards that fly apart.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from Burn-My-Windows by Simon Schneegans, https://github.com/Schneegans/Burn-My-Windows)

name: Energize A
description: A Star Trek transporter dematerialisation. The window dissolves through a shimmering atom shower with a central heart-glow
author: PlasmaZones

name: Energize B
description: A Star Trek transporter beam-up. A horizontal shower wave passes through the window, leaving vertical beam-streaks and shimmering atoms in its wake
author: PlasmaZones

name: Fire
description: BMW's flagship fire effect. An animated procedural fire texture eats the surface from top to bottom.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from Burn-My-Windows by Simon Schneegans, https://github.com/Schneegans/Burn-My-Windows)

name: Heat Melt
description: A heat-driven melt where simplex noise carves the surface away from the bottom-right corner with radial falloff.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Incinerate
description: A heat-driven dissolve with embers and chromatic distortion.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from Burn-My-Windows by Simon Schneegans, https://github.com/Schneegans/Burn-My-Windows)

name: Ink Splash
description: An ink-blot reveal where an fbm-distorted radial threshold blooms outward like spilled ink.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Inkwell Drop
description: A circular ink front spreads from the point of impact with concentric ringed distortion.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Phosphor Condense
description: The window condenses out of rising ember dust in the Phosphor style. Sparks drift upward and thicken along a noisy frontier that climbs the surface, each region locking into the image as the light reaches it, with the brand gradient from cyan to rose riding the embers. Closing disperses the window back into embers that burn out as they rise.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Phosphor Transfer
description: Switching tabs in a scrolling column breaks the old tab up into embers that re-settle as the new one. A ragged frontier climbs the column and the material comes apart along it, brightest right where the handover is happening, with the brand gradient from cyan to rose riding the sparks. Both tabs stay fully covered the whole way, so the column never shows the desktop behind it.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Phosphor Vortex
description: Grab a window and a plasma vortex around the cursor inhales it, pulling the surface into glowing streamlines that erode as they feed in. The plasma keeps orbiting for as long as the drag is held, stretches into a comet along the path while you move, and releases the window back when you let go.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Smoke
description: Domain-warped fbm smoke. The surface dissipates into curling smoke, with different formulas for reveal and dissolve.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Snap
description: A Thanos-style snap. The surface shatters into 10 randomized layers that fly toward a vanishing point, with different direction and re-form curves.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Wisps
description: Sparse animated noise trails dissipate the surface like smoke wisps.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from Burn-My-Windows by Simon Schneegans, https://github.com/Schneegans/Burn-My-Windows)

name: Strip Jelly
description: The strip wobbles like a soft body while it scrolls. The rows to either side of the strip's middle lag behind it, so the content bows in the direction of travel and relaxes straight as the strip settles.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Wobbly Move
description: Drag transition that turns the window into a sheet of fabric held at the point you grab, so the rest drapes and trails behind, driven by a neighbour-coupled spring simulation. Every physics knob is exposed so the feel can be dialled from taut cloth to loose jelly.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Desktop Pixelate
description: Cross-fades between desktops through a mosaic of pixel blocks that grow then shrink.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from GL-Transitions pixelize by gre, MIT)

name: Doom
description: Pixel columns melt downward at noise-randomized speeds, sliding off the bottom edge
author: PlasmaZones

name: Pixel Wheel
description: A pixelated clockwise spoke dissolve. Pixels fade away in spinning wedge sectors around the window centre
author: PlasmaZones

name: Pixel Wipe
description: Pixelated radial dissolve emanating from a configurable origin point
author: PlasmaZones

name: Pixelate
description: Progressive pixelation transition that dissolves into blocks
author: PlasmaZones

name: Pixelfade Wave
description: Wave-front pixelation where block size pulses along a diagonal wave that sweeps across the surface.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Desktop Circle
description: Reveals the incoming desktop through a growing circle, or closes the outgoing one into a shrinking circle.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Desktop Phosphor
description: Switches desktops over a circuit of light in the official Phosphor style. Signal pulses race along glowing traces in the switch direction, nodes flare as each pulse arrives, and the new desktop floods outward from every lit node behind a thin front carrying the brand gradient.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Desktop Wipe
description: Sweeps the incoming desktop across the screen behind a soft edge.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Genie
description: Minimize transition modeled on the classic genie lamp. The window stretches toward its task manager icon, with the edge nearest the icon leading the pour, and slips inside. Restoring plays the same motion back out of the icon. A window without a task manager entry collapses into its own bottom edge instead.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Peek Blinds
description: Splits the screen into venetian slats that tilt open one after another, so the windows collapse to thin bands and the desktop shows through as the reveal sweeps across.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Phosphor Bloom
description: The window fills with light along a diagonal sweep in the official Phosphor style. Ahead of the front the surface is a dark navy silhouette, and the front itself carries the brand gradient from cyan to rose with a soft shimmering glow.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Phosphor Gate
description: Edge gates for the scrolling strip in the official Phosphor style. Columns arriving on screen materialize through a cyan energize gate at the edge they enter from, and columns leaving drain to a dark navy silhouette with a rose afterglow at the edge they leave by. The gates breathe in with scroll speed and never touch the middle of the screen. Everything settles to the plain strip the instant scrolling stops.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Phosphor Ignition
description: The window ignites from its centre in the Phosphor style. A plasma bloom expands outward behind a turbulent rim of brand light with soft tendrils reaching ahead of it, the image shimmers briefly where the heat has just passed, and the rim carries the gradient from cyan at the core to rose at the corners. Closing collapses the plasma back into the centre.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Phosphor Iris
description: A ring of plasma opens from the centre of a scrolling column and swaps its tabs, in the Phosphor style. Inside the ring the tab you picked has already formed, while outside it the tab you left drains toward a dark navy silhouette as the ring closes on it. The rim is turbulent and carries the brand gradient from cyan at the centre to rose at the corners, with soft tendrils reaching ahead of it and ember sparks shed in its wake. Once the ring clears the corners the swap is done and nothing glows.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Phosphor Peek
description: Reveals the desktop in the official Phosphor style. The windows de-energize like a circuit shutting down, a front sweeps across along glowing traces, and the pixels drain along them into the brand gradient as the desktop is left behind.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Phosphor Scan
description: The window powers on like a phosphor screen. A bright beam scans down the surface leaving a glowing persistence trail that settles into the image, faint scanlines fade as the picture stabilises, and the beam carries the brand gradient from cyan to rose. Closing powers the screen back down through the same scan.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Phosphor Siphon
description: The window is siphoned into its task manager icon as separated luminous streams. Each stream runs on its own slightly offset clock and bows apart mid flight, carrying a different stop of the brand gradient, with ember sparks shed in the wake. Each region fades into the icon as it arrives, and restoring pours the streams back out. A window without a task manager entry drains into its own bottom edge instead.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Tab Wipe
description: Sweeps the tab you picked across the column over the one you left, with a soft edge you can widen into a gradient or tighten to a hard line. Neither tab moves, so the column stays put while its contents change.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Bounce
description: The window drops in from above the frame with a decaying bounce.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Desktop Slide
description: Slides the incoming desktop in as the outgoing one slides out.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from GL-Transitions directional by gre, MIT)

name: Desktop Slide & Fade
description: Slides the desktops a short way while cross-fading between them, the way Hyprland's slidefade switches workspaces.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Directional Wipe
description: Diagonal soft-edge wipe with smoothstep falloff.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Fly-In
description: Translates the surface in from the closest horizontal screen edge.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Glide
description: Smooth slide-and-fade glide entrance/exit.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from Burn-My-Windows by Simon Schneegans, https://github.com/Schneegans/Burn-My-Windows)

name: Paint Brush
description: Paint-stroke wipe across the surface.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from Burn-My-Windows by Simon Schneegans, https://github.com/Schneegans/Burn-My-Windows)

name: Pop In
description: Scale-from-center pop-in with overshoot and opacity fade
author: PlasmaZones

name: Slide
description: Directional slide transition with configurable direction
author: PlasmaZones

name: Slide Fade
description: Combined slide and opacity fade transition with soft edge
author: PlasmaZones

name: Tab Slide
description: Pushes the tab you left out of the column while the one you picked follows it in, like sliding a card out of a stack and the next one into its place. The stronger of the two direction settings picks the axis, so the slide is horizontal or vertical, and you can point it at whichever edge the tab bar sits on.
author: PlasmaZones

name: TV Effect
description: An old-CRT power-off. The window collapses vertically to a horizontal line, then horizontally to a point, then flashes
author: PlasmaZones

name: Wave Warp
description: A soft directional wave wipe with scale-warp. The surface contracts inward as it sweeps across. A Front Speed of 1 or higher lets the wipe complete early and hold revealed. This subsumes the former crosswarp shader.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Crosshatch
description: A crosshatch reveal using a random diagonal threshold with radial falloff from the center.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Hexagon
description: A Tron-style hex-tile dissolve. The window splits into shrinking hexagonal tiles overlaid with glowing edge lines
author: PlasmaZones

name: Honeycomb
description: A hexagonal-grid radial wipe where cells reveal and hide from the centre outward
author: arch-disciple, ported by PlasmaZones

name: Perlin
description: A Perlin-noise threshold reveal where the surface appears as noise crosses the rising progress threshold.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Polar Function
description: A polar petal reveal where an n-fold cosine radial mask grows outward with progress.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Polka Dots Curtain
description: A polka-dots curtain where the reveal threshold scales with distance from the origin, so dots open faster near a corner.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Random Squares
description: A random-grid block reveal where each cell flips on at its own threshold with a soft window.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Voronoi Shatter
description: A Voronoi-cell shatter where each shard reveals at its own threshold using a per-cell hash.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from liixini/shaders, https://github.com/liixini/shaders)

name: Desktop Cross Zoom
description: Zooms and blurs the outgoing desktop into the incoming one for a cinematic switch.
author: PlasmaZones (ported from GL-Transitions CrossZoom by rectalogic, MIT)

name: Peek Recede
description: Shrinks the windows toward a chosen point and fades them out as they darken, so they recede into depth and reveal the desktop behind them.
author: PlasmaZones

name: Tab Zoom
description: Pulls the tab you left toward you as it fades, while the one you picked rises from just behind it. The two are always at different depths, so the swap reads as a change of focus rather than a change of place.
author: PlasmaZones
